title: tabcheck/1: deterministic checks of an aligned feature table
description: Fifteen measurements of a .mzfeat table, each with the value, the threshold it is read against, a flag, up to 20 example rows and the numbers used. Computed by crates/mzlab-feat/src/tabcheck.rs (same table and options, same bytes; at most 6000 estimated tokens, ceil(bytes / 3)). Numbers only: a flagged row is a candidate to look at, never an identification. A check that lacks what it needs (a blank, QC files, accurate mass) is a note with value null and proof {missing}.

considered.description: rows of the view, or all of them

samples.description: files that are neither blank, QC nor dark

fwhm_min.description: median FWHM of the detected peaks, minutes: the RT window in which two rows co-elute

high_resolution.description: false when the m/z tolerance of the alignment is 0.1 Da or more (unit resolution: isotopes one Da apart, no Kendrick series)

truncated.description: the example rows and pairs were cut to keep the text inside the token cap; the checks are all there

checks.description: always in this order: size, blank, contaminants, qc_cv, qc_intensity, rt_drift, duplicates, adducts, isotopes, insource, long_traces, homologous, missing, structure, polarity_units

value.description: what was measured (a share, a count, a CV, a change, a shift in minutes, a correlation); null when the check could not be made

threshold.description: the limit the value is read against; the other limits of the check are in proof

rows.description: ids of the table (1-based position), the most telling first; for a pair the heavier row comes first

files.description: names of the files the check points at

proof.description: the numbers used: counts, shares, the other limits, up to 5 pairs {lo, hi, dmz, drt, kind, r} (adducts: kind is the adduct, r the correlation of the areas; isotopes: obs_over_expected; insource: parents with their fragments; homologous: unit, members, consecutive, rho), or {missing} naming what the check lacked (blank, qc, files, groups, common_rows, high_resolution, widths, rows, pca, or the key of the PCA error)
